bib.title: LLM-BLENDER: Ensembling Large Language Models with Pairwise Ranking and Generative Fusion
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2023), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 14165-14178

read.skipped: The PDF has 14 pages and ends at the ACL checklist; the appendices the text cites (prompt template, aggregator ablation, summarization/translation/CommonGen results, hyperparameters, metrics) are not in this file, so none of it could be read.

question: Can the complementary strengths of many open-source instruction-tuned LLMs be combined per input by ranking their outputs pairwise and fusing the top ones, beating any single fixed LLM?
hypothesis: Optimal LLMs vary per example, so dynamically ensembling (rank then fuse) gives consistently better outputs than any fixed model; pairwise joint encoding discriminates subtle candidate differences better than pointwise scoring.
contributions: A new framework: LLM-BLENDER, a post-hoc ensemble method for ranking and fusing outputs from multiple LLMs (PAIRRANKER and GENFUSER).
A new dataset: MixInstruct, a benchmark for training and evaluating LLM ensembling on instruction-following tasks.

method.summary: Run N=11 open-source LLMs on every input, compare all candidate pairs with a cross-attention ranker (PairRanker, DeBERTa 400m) that jointly encodes the input and two candidates, aggregate the pairwise logit matrix into a ranking, then feed the top K=3 candidates with the input to GenFuser (Flan-T5-XL 3b) which generates the final answer. Evaluated on MixInstruct with BERTScore, BARTScore, BLEURT and a ChatGPT pairwise-comparison rank (GPT-Rank).
method.task: ensembling LLM outputs for instruction following (rank-and-fuse, post-hoc)

datasets.name: MixInstruct
datasets.size: 110K examples (Alpaca-GPT4 22,862; Dolly-15K 7,584; GPT4All-LAION 76,552; ShareGPT 3,002); mean I/O tokens 20 / 66
datasets.source: four open instruction datasets, formatted as self-instruct; candidates from 11 LLMs; oracle pairwise labels from ChatGPT on the test set
datasets.preprocessing: curated and processed open-source data; ground truth shown to ChatGPT in pairwise comparisons; train/val use BERTScore, BLEURT, BARTScore against ground truth

models.name: PairRanker
models.architecture: DeBERTa (He et al., 2021) cross-attention encoder; input '<s><source> x </s> <candidate1> yi </s> <candidate2> yj </s>'; special-token embeddings concatenated and passed to a single-head MLP whose last dimension equals the number of Q functions

models.name: GenFuser
models.architecture: Flan-T5-XL seq2seq; input is x plus K top candidates joined by <extra_id_i> separators

models.name: 11 candidate LLMs (Open Assistant, Vicuna, Alpaca, Baize, MOSS, ChatGLM, Koala, Dolly V2, Mosaic MPT, StableLM, Flan-T5)

other.sizes: not stated in the main text

other.use: pairwise comparison of 55 pairs per example, ties allowed; oracle ranking and GPT-Rank

training.objective: PairRanker: multi-task pairwise BCE, L_Q = -z_i log sigma(s_i^(i,j)) - (1-z_j) log sigma(s_j^(i,j)), averaged over Q functions; Q chosen as BARTScore for main runs. GenFuser: fine-tune Flan-T5-XL to generate the ground truth y.
training.regularisation: candidate order shuffled within each training pair

other.pairs_per_input: 5 sampled pairs per input in training, out of N(N-1)/2
other.ground_truth: ground truth y mixed into the candidate pool during training
other.appendix: Checklist says hyperparameters and compute are in Appendix A, which is not in this PDF

inference.samples: one candidate per LLM per input (N=11); no seeds or repeated runs stated
inference.prompting: not stated for candidate generation in the main text; ChatGPT comparison prompt template is in the appendix (not in this PDF)

parameters.aggregators: MaxLogits (s_i = sum(M_i* - M_*i)), MaxWins (count of wins), bubble-sort single pass (O(N) comparisons)

metrics.name: BERTScore
metrics.definition: similarity of output to ground truth

metrics.name: BARTScore
metrics.definition: generation-likelihood based similarity to ground truth

metrics.name: GPT-Rank
metrics.definition: ChatGPT pairwise comparisons on all candidates; rank by number of wins (MaxWins); average rank

metrics.name: Vic / OA (%)
metrics.definition: percent of examples where output is better than or as good as Vicuna / Open Assistant by GPT-Rank

metrics.name: Top-3 (%)
metrics.definition: percent of examples where output ranks in the top 3 by GPT-Rank

metrics.name: Pearson / Spearman / Spearman's Footrule
metrics.definition: rank correlation of a ranking method with the GPT-Rank oracle ranking

baselines: oracle selections by BERTScore, BLEURT, BARTScore, GPT-Rank
eval.protocol: Single run on the 5k test set; no error bars or significance tests; judge is ChatGPT shown the ground truth; no human evaluation.

results.claim: Full pairwise comparison costs O(N^2) inferences; a single bubble-sort pass cuts it to O(N) (N-1 comparisons).
results.note: Appendix reports the cost/accuracy trade-off; not in this PDF.

limits: Full PairRanker needs O(n^2) model calls; authors say they can run in parallel and bubble sort reduces cost, but no latency, cost or compute numbers are given in the main text.
Evaluation uses ChatGPT (shown ground truth) as judge, no large-scale human evaluation; authors concede automatic metrics are limited.
Only 11 open-source models of 2023; no comparison to closed models like GPT-4 or to cheaper routing; all N models must be run for every input, so it is an ensemble not a cost-saving router.
Training hyperparameters, compute, decoding settings and the judge prompt are in an appendix absent from the supplied PDF.
Single run, no seeds or significance tests.

terms.definition: Selection-based methods compare candidates in the set Y, selecting the top-ranked candidate as the final output
fusing K candidates (1 < K <= N) from Y to produce an unseen response as the final output
ChatGPT pairwise comparisons on all candidates, ranked by number of wins (MaxWins aggregation)
confidence that y_i is superior to all other candidates: sum of row minus column of the comparison matrix
number of victories in comparisons with other candidates

lineage.note: pointwise reranker, cosine similarity of input and candidate
fusion idea; Ravaut et al. 2022b fused summaries without a prior selection step
pointwise scoring with pairwise loss; contrasted with pairwise inference

code.snippet: L_Q = -z_i log sigma(s_i^(i,j)) - (1 - z_j) log sigma(s_j^(i,j))
MaxLogits: s_i = sum(M_i* - M_*i); MaxWins: s_i = |{s_ij in M_i* | s_ij > 0}| + |{s_ji in M_*i | s_ji < 0}|
